LESSON: ENERGY, WORK, POWER AND MACHINES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Mechanics and Thermal Physics
Topic 1.6: Energy, Work, Power and Machines
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Energy, Work, Power and Machines, part of Mechanics and Thermal Physics in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How do machines make work easier?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Energy, Work, Power and Machines together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: the learner develops the ability to communicate effectively with team members as

they work well together in every situation and empathize with each other as they recognize the value of others ideas

while discussing with peers and explaining the meaning of the terms used in Physics.

36

Critical thinking and problem solving: the learner develops the evaluation and decision making skill while they explore

complex problems by identifying when there are no technical solutions as they solve problems involving energy, work

done, power and machines in day-to-day life (velocity ratio, mechanical advantage & efficiency).

Values

• Love: the learner shares information with others by portraying a caring attitude while working with others to construct

simple machines.

• Responsibility: as the learner shows accountability by caring for own property and those of others while performing

experiments to demonstrate mechanical energy transformations and forms of potential energy.

Values:

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills and values education

• Socio-Economic and Environmental education: the learner appreciates environment and technology as they use

technology in managing the environment while performing experiments to demonstrate mechanical energy

transformations and forms of potential energy.

• General history of Africa: as the learner appreciates the development of machines from simple to complex machines /

evolution of machines from archaic to modern (e.g. steam engine to electric engines).

Suggested learning resources;

Machines, levers, inclined planes, pulleys, wheel and axle, pulley belt, functioning motor vehicle, catapult, bow and

arrow. Hydraulic lift, screw

Suggested key skill;

demonstrate the transformation of mechanical energy using simple apparatus
